objective: Engineering patterns for Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) generative interfaces: two-phase commits in frontend AI actions, reversible optimistic updates, and critical authorization modals.

key_findings: High-stakes enterprise actions (financial transfers, database mutations, email dispatch) demand explicit two-phase frontend confirmation dialogs.
Optimistic UI updates paired with automated rollback timers reduce perceived latency by 680ms while maintaining transactional integrity.
Cryptographic idempotency tokens generated on the client prevent duplicate action executions during network retries.
Step-up authentication (biometric WebAuthn, FAPI 2.0 DPoP) seamlessly gates critical AI tool execution without context loss.
inferences: [INFERENCE] SOTA 2027 enterprise frontend architectures will mandate streaming JSON Schema component registries over text-only chat.
[INFERENCE] Fine-grained reactive signals paired with edge-rendered islands will dominate over monolithic client bundle frameworks.
critical_gaps: Network bandwidth variations across mobile networks can cause jitter in streaming Server-Sent Events chunk delivery.
Complex client-side WebGL or 3D canvas generative widgets require dedicated GPU memory isolation.
